S01.in_words: The column is the ordinal of a value on the located row (extract.py:604-606) and the id is built from it with no name (extract.py:705-706). The producer holds who the columns are outside the page: the primary portfolio's name (recipe.py:919, cover primary_name) and the chosen comparison securities, in request order (recipe.py:306 comparisons in key order; publisher.py:88-100 _chosen_comparisons, names in key order). The only use made of those names after the vendor renders is an existence test that each name is printed somewhere in the PDF text (certify.py:120-133 missing_comparison_names; resident_worker.py:511-530; publisher.py:252-256). Nothing joins a name, or the name's position, to a column ordinal, and extract.extract is not handed the names (extract.py:623 takes pdf_bytes and census only). The census values for this section are keyed by the two entities (census line 178). The census block for S01 has no axes entry (S01 spans census lines 178-223), so a printed heading for this section is not shown by the census.

S14.in_words: The columns are the periods of ONE row: _row_values takes the numbers to the right of the label on the same line, left to right, up to six (extract.py:556,596,603-606), and extract stops at the first label hit that has values (extract.py:662-668), so the ordinal is a period position on that one row. The census records the period headings the page prints for this section as axes.window (census line 1433 onward: five headings), so the labels are on the rendered page. No code reads them: census_field_rows copies section, field, unit, group, pages and values (extract.py:246-254) and never the section's axes; the word axes is read by no source under investor-reporting/. The synthetic fixtures do not show these headings: for a per-entity list value they print the marker '[see table]' (fixtures/synthetic_pdf/generate.py:96-97). Which entity's row the first hit is, is not stated by the id either.

column_order_claim.in_words: No code ties the ordinal to the request's security order: the request order exists on the producer side only (recipe.py:306, 880-890, publisher.py:88-100) and is checked only for printed existence (certify.py:120-133). What the ordinal follows is the page, and only partly. On a same-line row the candidates are sorted by x0, so the ordinal is a left-to-right rank (extract.py:597,603). But the rank counts only tokens that parse as a number, a missing token or an undecoded glyph (extract.py:587-595: any other token is skipped with continue), so one unreadable cell shifts every later column one place left under the same id pattern. On the BELOW layout (value stacked under the label) the candidates are sorted by their top coordinate (extract.py:598-599,603), so the ordinal is top-to-bottom, not left-to-right. The list is cut at six (extract.py:556,603). The synthetic fixtures print columns in the producer's order (fixtures/synthetic_pdf/generate.py:68-73,142-143), which is order by construction and not a measurement of the vendor.

stored_report.address_rule_in_words: A finished vendor report is the ANALYSIS record that CertifiedReportPublisher.publish persists through ReportRepository.persist (ycharts/generate/publisher.py:280; reports/repository.py:185-216): report_id is RPT- plus the first 32 hex of the digest of owner, kind and request id (repository.py:134-141), revision is the sha256 of the canonical record (repository.py:202), and S3ReportBlobs.put (repository.py:535-549) asks the destination callback for (bucket, key). That callback is opal_naming.reporting_destination (lib/opal_naming.py:2476-2481, _reporting_destination 2458-2473): key(policy source, firm, tier, table, report_id) + '/' + sha256 + '.' + extension, which for the ANALYSIS family of policy irpt-x10-v1 (infra/logic/registry/reporting_policies.json) is tier platinum, table analysis_reports, extension json: irpt/<firm>/platinum/analysis_reports/RPT-<32 hex>/<sha256>.json in the product bucket. The record holds report.sections (dated) and report.undated_sections, both carrying section ids (ycharts/extract/publication.py:217-218).
stored_report.list_result: list-objects-v2 under irpt/<firm>/platinum/analysis_reports/ for each of the 3 firms the policy registers: rc 0 each; 1, 20 and 0 objects; 21 in all; no truncation flag.
stored_report.refusal_in_words: The one get-object, of the newest of the 21 objects by LastModified, returned AccessDenied: the dell2 agent user is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on the object's key. The list was allowed, the read of a body was not. Per the face's refusal clause no other object, identity or path was tried, so no stored report was read, no section id was counted, and whether any stored report carries S18 sections was not established. Row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-W324-S1.

consumers_of_the_section_id_shape.in_words: Builds the vendor id as '<census section code>.<slug of the field label>.c<column ordinal>'; the only place the column ordinal enters the id.
Builds the chart row id '<code>.chart.<slug of the section title>' for a section with zero field rows; no column part.
undated_rows lists up to 40 held-out ids in its provenance array; the id is copied, not read.
date_claim_census collects the ids of rows whose date does not match their provenance (also :996); the id is carried as a label.
_grade_row copies the id into the grade record (also :484, :553, :600 in the controls).
The forced-undecoded control builds '<code>.<slug>.FORCED' from an unlocated record's section code and field, a test-only id variant with no column part.
emitted_glyph_census scans the id string for a raw (cid: occurrence; it reads the characters, not the shape.
The chart fragment row copies the id unchanged.

_unique refuses DUPLICATE_SOURCE_ROW when two rows (sections plus charts) have the same whole id. This is the one place two cards of a field must differ in the id, and it relies on the c<column> suffix to differ.

Matches a unit conflict to its row by the tuple (section code, label, column, page) from the private keys _label and _column, NOT by parsing the id; the private keys are dropped before the wire (publication.py:215-216), so on the wire the id is the only carrier of the column.
Gap records name the id (also :193) as 'id'; the id is copied.
section_dates takes each row's id as an identity for the dated census; requires a string of length 1 to 200 and refuses a repeated id (:59-61). It does not parse the id.
The status verifier checks each census row is exactly {section_id, as_of_date}, the id a string of length 1 to 200 and not repeated (:370-374).
Contract v1: section_id is type string with no pattern, length or enum; also :199 (the undated item refs it). The shape is not in the contract.
Contract v2, ycharts branch: type string, no pattern (also :214 the undated ref, :640 the Opal branch).
Status envelope section date row: string, minLength 1, maxLength 200 (:169-171); a length bound only. The public envelope has the same bound at PublicStatusEnvelope.schema.json:167-170.
The published contract copy of the report section id: same as the service copy, no pattern (also :199).
The published copy of the status envelope row: string, 1 to 200 (also PublicStatusEnvelope.schema.json:167).
Test finds a row by whole-id equality to edit its reason (also :68, :71).
Test appends a copy of a row and expects DUPLICATE_SOURCE_ROW from the whole-id uniqueness check.
Test builds rows with free-form ids ('S-WEIGHT-1', 'd', 'u') and asserts whole-id equality of section_dates output (:22-28, :38-63); no vendor-shaped id appears.
Test builds the ids 'dated' and 'undated', and empty or short ones at :133-135 for the length bound; free-form ids.
Test builds 'S-RET-%d' ids (also test_submit_analysis_branch.py:37, test_retained_export_analysis.py:35); free-form, not the S<code>.<slug>.c<n> shape.
Test overwrites an id with 'undated-source-row'; free-form.
